Additionally, she worked with a child therapist to help her explain Randall’s condition to her children. She said Louis and Laila noticed the physical change in Randall and handled it differently. While Louis realized about two years before Bryan’s death that he needed to step away, Laila stayed involved until around six months before he died.

“I was able to sort of wall off a whole section (of my house) and make it a different entrance where it had an outside garden and all these kinds of things,” she said about managing to keep the children away from the situation when they asked.
Bullock said she looks back at that time in her life and sees the toll it took on her. In some red carpet photos of herself, she notices her skin looks gray.
“I just felt there was this black shroud over me. Going, if my curse, which is the minute I say something about this, I don’t want anyone else to be blamed for something,” she explained.
She felt “relief” when she finally confided in her friends.

While she said Randall would have to be the one to explain why he wanted his illness to be kept a secret, she added, “I think where he was in his journey, both physically and mentally, I started grieving Bryan four years before he passed. Like something in my head said, ‘Start the grieving now.’ Because I knew I would be the caregiver, and I could see, like, the bright eyes that I knew … there was something that had shifted.”

She continued, “It is a traumatic diagnosis. Anyone who can prevail through a diagnosis like that, I bow down. You know, my mother had cancer. We always had hope. You always have hope that there’s something. But I could see that there was a darkness.”
Bullock revealed that she had lingering “guilt” from Randall’s death up until about a year ago. She said as a mother she felt guilty that her children had to experience such a difficult time.

“Then someone said to me, you know, ‘If you believe children choose you, they also choose this journey. This journey is for them, as well,’” she said. “That sort of took a little weight off my shoulders.”
Still, she said she apologized to them for what happened.
Bullock and Randall, a model turned photographer, met in 2015 when he was hired to snap photos for Louis’ birthday party.
“He’s the love of my life,” Bullock gushed about Randall in a 2021 interview on “Red Table Talk.”

“I am someone who went through the divorce process. I found the love of my life,” she said at the time. “We share two beautiful children — three children, his older daughter. It’s the best thing ever. I don’t want to say, ‘Do it how I do it.’ But I don’t need a paper to be a devoted partner and a devoted mother.”

title: Charlamagne Tha God Tells a Craig Melvin Story That Has Jenna and Sheinelle in Tears
summary: Charlamagne tha God told Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones a funny story about a time he hung out with Craig Melvin several years ago.
story: Charlamagne tha God knows Craig Melvin from way back when.

While appearing on the Aug. 19 episode of TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle, the “Breakfast Club” host regaled Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones with a funny tale about Craig back when they were both coming up the ranks in their professions back in South Carolina.
“Craig is one of the most disciplined people,” he said.
Charlamagne then provided a story to illustrate just how disciplined Craig is.

“I remember we used to hang out at this club called V12 in Columbia, South Carolina. And I remember us being, I think it was my birthday party or something, so we’re in the VIP (area), and, you know, we’re just sitting back there cooling, and somebody in the club was smoking marijuana.”
Charlamagne said Craig’s reaction was swift and definitive.
“And I remember Craig going (makes sniffing sound), ‘Is that marijuana? Charlamagne, I gotta go!’” he said, while Jenna and Sheinelle cracked up.
“And he got up and skedaddled out of the club. He was gone. He’s always been one of the most disciplined people I’ve ever known.”

Sheinelle said Craig often gets teased for being friends with someone as “cool” as Charlamagne tha God. Jenna added in that Craig would “be the first to admit he was a little bit of a nerd” as a well-known throwback picture of him holding a violin appeared on the screen.
“I got a picture worse than that,” the radio star jumped in to say.

“Back in the day when we were in Columbia, South Carolina, I was doing radio on Hot 103.9. He was on WIS, and there was a guy named Otis Taylor Jr. who wrote for the state newspaper, and he did like this ‘top 10 people in arts and entertainment in South Carolina under the age of 25.’ Me and Craig was in there, and Craig is laying in like a grassy knoll with a golden retriever licking his face.”
The thought of that image was too much for Jenna and Sheinelle.
“I will give you $12,” Sheinelle said.
Charlamagne said he has the picture “laminated somewhere,” which only piqued Jenna and Sheinelle’s interest further.
“Please find that,” Jenna said. “We will pay you $24.”

title: Here’s Why Robin Williams’ Children Just Revived His Instagram Account
summary: Robin Williams’ three children are honoring his legacy in a unique way by starting a new instagram page.  Here’s what to know.
story: Robin Williams’ three children are honoring his legacy in a unique way.

His sons Zak and Cody and daughter Zelda Williams revived the late actor’s Instagram account on Aug. 18, telling fans in a statement that they wanted to create a “trusted” space to share stories about their father. It comes over a decade after Williams died by suicide in 2014 while suffering from Lewy body dementia. He was 63.
Their statement, shared on Williams’ account, appeared to be a response to the growing amount of AI-generated images and videos that have featured the comedian’s likeness in recent years.

“As we recognize what would be our Dad’s 75th year, we’re grateful to see new generations discovering his work while longtime fans continue to celebrate the joy he brought into their lives,” said the statement, signed by Zak, 43, Cody, 34 and Zelda Williams, 37. “As technology evolves, we want this to be a safe, trusted place where the stories, photos, videos, and memories shared reflect his legacy with authenticity, warmth, and care.”

Robin Williams, whose birthday would’ve been roughly a month ago on July 21, established himself as a cinema icon through his critically acclaimed performances in hits like 1989’s “Dead Poets Society,” 1993’s “Mrs. Doubtfire” and 1997’s “Good Will Hunting.” Since his death, his social media pages have remained untouched.

However, fans have continued to remember the comedian — at-times through the controversial means of using AI to create deepfake videos. In late 2025, the now-defunct video creation Sora app — a product of OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT —  came under fire after late celebrities, including Robin Williams, appeared in unauthorized videos that were made by users.
At the time, Zelda Williams slammed the deepfakes of her father, calling for an end to the videos.

“If you’re just trying to troll me, I’ve seen way worse, I’ll restrict and move on. But please, if you’ve got any decency, just stop doing this to him and to me, to everyone even, full stop,” she wrote on Oct. 7 in her Instagram stories.

She added: “To watch the legacies of real people be condensed down to, ‘This vaguely looks and sounds like them so that’s enough,’ just so other people can churn out horrible TikTok slop puppeteering them is maddening.”
In the new post on their father’s Instagram account, the siblings said that the page would serve as one means of keeping Robin Williams’ legacy alive.

“This is our way of sharing his unique talent and humor with the world, including the moments that made us and so many of you laugh, as we remember our Dad’s extraordinary life and work,” the three siblings said in the statement. “He continues to inspire us and delight people all over the world.”

title: Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s Wedding Bands Analyzed by a Jewelry Pro
summary: Pictures came out of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding rings. Jewelers took a look and analyzed.
story: Taylor Swift’s stunning engagement ring just got a new neighbor.
Six weeks ago, the “Opalite” singer and Travis Kelce said “I do” in an epic wedding celebration at Madison Square Garden in New York City.
The newlyweds have managed to lay low for the most part over the last few weeks, but they were both spotted sporting their wedding bands at separate events over the last few days.

Per People, Swift attended the wedding of recording engineers Oli Jacobs and Laura Sisk in the U.K. over the weekend. At the event, photographers caught a photo of the swinger’s gold wedding band, which paired perfectly with her engagement ring.
Kelce, who is already back to work preparing for the upcoming NFL season with the Kansas City Chiefs, was seen rocking his own gold wedding band at his team’s first preseason game.
During an Aug. 12 press conference at the Kansas City Chiefs’ training camp practice, Kelce broke his silence on his wedding, saying he had a “fun offseason.”
“The wedding was the best night of my life, and I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and had fun with us,” he said.
Eager to learn more about the newlyweds’ wedding bands? TODAY.com consulted a few jewelry pros to get all the details.
What Does Travis Kelce’s Wedding Ring look Like?
According to Melanie Fitzpatrick, co-founder of LeMel, a Houston-based fine jewelry brand, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end chose a “classic, solid gold yellow band.”
Based on the gold’s warmth and rich tone, Fitzpatrick thinks the band is made of 18K gold. It appears to be 8 mm wide, she says.
“Travis is almost always wearing gold jewelry and gold watches, so a gold band feels very on-brand for him,” she says.
What Does Taylor Swift’s Wedding Band Look Like?
Like Kelce’s, Swift’s wedding ring is made of yellow gold, but with more embellishments.
Looking at a variety of photos of Swift’s ring, Fitzpatrick noticed that the front of the wedding band has round diamonds, while the back is made of plain gold.
Fitzpatrick believes the wedding band was custom made to fit her engagement ring, designed by Kindred Lubeck.

“This is probably my favorite detail. Her band was clearly designed specifically around her engagement ring. The fact that the band sits completely flush with her engagement ring is such a thoughtful detail. It really lets the two rings come together as one cohesive piece and accentuates the engagement ring without taking anything away from it,” Fitzpatrick says.
Swift’s engagement ring has a old mine cushion cut diamond center stone. The band is hand-carved by Lubeck, a jeweler who was at Swift and Kelce’s wedding.
Jewelers, in previous interviews with TODAY.com, estimated the ring is worth between $400,000 and $1.2 million.

title: ‘Sister Wives’ Star Christine Brown Reacts to Janelle’s New Boyfriend
summary: Janelle Brown debuted her new boyfriend and Christine Brown, her former sister wife, had something to say about it.
story: “Sister Wives” stars Janelle and Christine Brown are celebrating each other as they enter new relationships.
For years, Janelle and Christine were sister wives, both married to Kody Brown, along with Robyn Brown and Meri Brown. The TLC show tracked the dissolution of three of his four marriages.
Today, Kody is only married to Robyn, whom he married fourth in 2010.
Christine has since moved on with David Woolley, whom she married in 2023.
On Aug. 18, Janelle Brown shared that she, too, had found love. She posted a photo of her with her new beau, Pete.

“Some chapters are meant to unfold quietly before they’re shared. I wasn’t looking. I certainly wasn’t expecting you. And somehow, you turned out to be exactly what I didn’t know I needed,” Janelle wrote. “And it has been pretty wonderful.”
In the comments of the post, Christine shared her support, writing what she thinks of Pete.
“He’s such an awesome guy!! They are so cute together and he’s a construction worker like David!!” she wrote.
Mykelti Padron, one of Christine and Kody’s daughters, shared her support in the comments, too: “I’m so happy for you!!”
Janelle and Kody announced they were splitting in late 2022, about a year after Christine and Kody broke up.
Janelle was present at Christine’s wedding to David in Moab, Utah, in October 2023.
In a joint interview with TODAY.com that occurred shortly after Christine’s wedding, Janelle expressed her excitement at her own new chapter.

“Life has been an unexpected journey. I didn’t expect to be here, reinventing myself at 50. I’m honored that people still want to see what I’m doing,” Janelle said. “Because I’m going to pull it off. I’m going to reinvent myself in a very big way. I hope that is inspiring to people.”
Meri Brown, Kody’s first wife, also debuted a new relationship in October 2023, but the two have since parted ways.

title: Vin Diesel Reflects on His Bond With Paul Walker’s Daughter Meadow: ‘I Would Die For Her’
summary: Just like Dom Toretto keeps his family close, so does Vin Diesel.
story: Just like Dom Toretto keeps his family close, so does Vin Diesel.
The actor, along with cast members from “The Fast and the Furious” reunited in Los Angeles on Aug. 17 to celebrate the action film’s 25th anniversary.
In attendance were also Michelle Rodriguez and Jordana Brewster, as well as the late Paul Walker’s 27-year-old daughter Meadow Walker.
Diesel expressed his love for his late friend’s daughter, sharing how having her in attendance gave him the fuel he needed to be at the special screening.
“It means everything,” Diesel told “Entertainment Tonight” about having Meadow Walker at the event. “Because I don’t know if I could have come to the red carpet.”
He recalled being at the original premiere 25 years ago “with my brother Pablo,” his nickname for the late Paul Walker. “I don’t know if the absence ... I would have been able to survive.”
“And Meadow adds a grace,” he continued, before sharing more insight about their bond.

“She’s the first one to ever call me on Father’s Day. She’s the first one to show up to all the kids’ birthdays,” Diesel said. “She’s just such a blessing and I’m so grateful to have her in my family’s life.”
He called her “a true cousin to my angels” and added, “I would die for her.”

Paul Walker died in a car crash in November 2013, his daughter was only 15 years old at the time. Since then, the “Fast and Furious” franchise has continued to honor the actor’s memory by including his character, Brian O’Conner, in the films, whether it’s with archival footage or mentions of what Brian has been up to.

As for Meadow Walker, she also made a cameo in 2023’s “Fast X” and attended the premiere. The model has been close with Diesel’s family and over the years has shared photos with the actor’s kids Hania, 18, Vincent, 16, and Pauline, 11, named after Paul Walker.
“It felt like a way to keep his memory a part of my family and a part of my world,” Diesel told TODAY in 2015 about his youngest daughter’s name.
Diesel is also Meadow Walker’s godfather and walked her down the aisle when she married actor Louis Thornton-Allan in 2021. She and Thornton-Allan announced their separation in 2023.
Meadow Walker had previously shared videos and photos of her with Diesel from her wedding, but they have since been deleted.

title: ‘Sister Wives’ Star Janelle Brown Goes Public with New Boyfriend 4 Years After Kody Brown Split
summary: “Sister Wives” star Janelle Brown has gone public with her new boyfriend, Pete, after her split from ex-husband Kody Brown.
story: Janelle Brown is celebrating a “pretty wonderful” chapter in her life.

The “Sister Wives” star shared a photo with her new beau on her Strive with Janelle Facebook page on Aug. 18. The relationship debut comes about four years after Janelle announced she was splitting from her ex-husband, Kody Brown.
Janelle and Kody’s marriage played out in the TLC show “Sister Wives,” alongside his marriages to Meri Brown, Christine Brown and Robyn Brown. He is currently only married to Robyn Brown.
Alongside the selfie, which shows the couple beaming, she shared a few words about how this new gent, referred to only as Pete, came into her life.

“Some chapters are meant to unfold quietly before they’re shared. I wasn’t looking. I certainly wasn’t expecting you. And somehow, you turned out to be exactly what I didn’t know I needed,” Janelle wrote. “And it has been pretty wonderful.”
Then, she rolled out the red carpet for her new partner: “Everyone please meet Pete.”
Janelle isn’t the only “sister wife” to have found love since leaving Kody. Christine Brown married David Woolley in 2023, months after they met, and the two are going strong.
In a previous interview with TODAY.com in 2023, a year after she announced she was leaving Kody, Janelle said she was embracing her “selfish” era.
“For once, I get to live for me,” Janelle says. “I get to do all those things I knew I was capable of. Now I get to do me and all the potential that’s there.”
At the time of the interview, she felt optimistic about what was to come.

“Life has been an unexpected journey. I didn’t expect to be here, reinventing myself at 50. I’m honored that people still want to see what I’m doing,” Janelle said. “Because I’m going to pull it off. I’m going to reinvent myself in a very big way. I hope that is inspiring to people.”

Since their split, she and Kody have faced a shared tragedy. One of their five children, Garrison, died in 2024. In the show, Garrison’s parents, siblings and relatives have honored his memory and shed light on his struggle with mental health. Janelle has been open with her grief journey, as well.
Despite “Sister Wives” showing their relationship hitting moments of turmoil, she said in a 2023 confessional that she didn’t regret marrying Kody.
“I know that I didn’t make a mistake in marrying him. I would do it all over again,” she said.

title: ‘Outer Banks’ Stars Share New Behind-the-Scenes Photos from Set, Reveal Stories Behind Them
summary: Chase Stokes, Drew Starkey and Jonathan Daviss reflect on never-before-seen photos from filming the hit Netflix adventure series.
story: The Pogues are back one last time.

Ahead of the Aug. 20 premiere of the fifth and final season of Netflix’s “Outer Banks,” the cast, who play a ragtag group of treasure-hunting teens, are reflecting on some behind-the-scenes treasures in their camera roll.

TODAY sat down with Chase Stokes, who stars as John B, Drew Starkey, who plays Rafe, and Jonathan Daviss, who portrays Pope, on Aug. 18. Each actor submitted one of their behind-the-scenes photos and shared the story behind it.
The first photo, sent in by Stokes, showed the three shadowed figures attempting (and for Daviss, admittedly failing) a jumping pose against a sunset-lit beach backdrop.
“I had about 30 of those photos, because we were trying to get it right, and that was the most awkward one,” Stokes explained.
For Starkey, his photo showed the morning after an impromptu cast bonding night from the beginning of the show’s journey. The cast found Stokes snug as a bug in a sleeping bag, sunglasses on.

“Funny story, our showrunner Jonas Pate put us together in the Chateau and said, ‘Just stay the night there, get to know each other,’ and we all crashed on the floor and couches, and little bedrooms, and we woke up in the morning and found Chase in that state,” Starkey said.
“I look like a little burrito!” Stokes chimed in, before giving the inside scoop on what led him to be in this position.

“The best part about it is that they did leave us with a couple cases of beer, and they didn’t tell me I had a screen test with cameras the next morning,” Stokes revealed. “So, they came with cameras, and they were like, ‘Alright, we’re just going to start shooting stuff,’ and I was like, ‘I am violently hungover and unwell.’”
For Daviss’ photo submission, the co-stars revisited an up-close and personal shot of Starkey in Croatia, where they filmed Season 5, and the photo left the three absolutely bursting with laughter.
“I have a bunch of these .5 photos I’ve taken of all the cast, and in that, Drew just looks pure evil,” Daviss said.
Still giggling, the boys challenge their cast mates, specifically upcoming TODAY guests Madelyn Cline, Madison Bailey and Carlacia Grant and to send in their own photos.
“If they’re real, they’ll do it,” Daviss said. “It’s the final season, girls.”

title: Jonathan Daviss Shares How Snoop Dogg’s Kids Reacted to Him Playing Their Dad in a Biopic
summary: Jonathan Daviss has been paid the ultimate compliment by Snoop Dogg’s four children as he prepares to play the iconic rapper in a biopic set to come out next year.
story: Jonathan Daviss has been paid the ultimate compliment by Snoop Dogg’s four children as he prepares to play the iconic rapper in a biopic set to come out next year.
The “Outer Banks” star spoke on TODAY Aug. 18 about embodying Snoop Dogg while also bearing a strong physical resemblance to the younger version of the 54-year-old entertainer.
“I’ve been with his kids and they’re like, ‘I feel I’m talking to my dad,’” Daviss said.

The biopic, titled “Snoop,” is scheduled to hit theaters on Aug. 6, 2027, according to The Hollywood Reporter. The rapper and beloved NBC Olympic commentator told Entertainment Tonight in June 2025 that the movie will follow his journey from adolescent struggles to rap stardom in the ‘90s, plus his relationship with wife Shante Broadus.

Daviss, 26, who was interviewed alongside “Outer Banks” castmates Chase Stokes and Drew Starkey on TODAY, also spoke about the intimidating audition process. He had to do his interpretation of Snoop Dogg with the rapper in the room.

“Terrifying,” Daviss said. “He’s sitting over there watching, and I’m like, ‘All right, I hope I’m doing this right.’ But he was so hands on and so open during that audition process, he really made me feel comfortable, like I could go all the way there. He gave me a lot of pointers, so really excited about that.”

Daviss and Snoop Dogg appeared onstage together at CinemaCon 2026 in Las Vegas in April to promote the biopic. Daviss wore a flannel shirt similar to the one the rapper wore in his iconic video for the 1993 hit “Who Am I (What’s My Name?).” The actor also had on a T-shirt featuring the cover of Snoop Dogg’s classic first solo album, “Doggstyle.”

Daviss experienced a surreal moment during his time at CinemaCon when he had dinner with Snoop Dogg and legendary actor Robert DeNiro. The photo was shared on Instagram by Death Row Pictures, which is helming the project as part of its overall deal with NBCUniversal Entertainment & Studios. (NBCUniversal is the parent company of TODAY)
“Coolest picture of my life,” Daviss said on TODAY.
“That’s the craziest thing I’ve ever seen,” Stokes added.
“We’re at Nobu with Robert DeNiro,” Daviss said. “I never guessed that in my life. I’m with The Godfather and Tha Doggfather.”
Snoop Dogg spoke with Entertainment Tonight in 2025 about choosing Daviss for the role in the biopic.

“He’s the whole thing,” the rapper said. “He’s a dynamic actor, he’s a great spirit, and he’s a learner. It’s just a beautiful thing to be able to find somebody that can actually do justice to you while you’re still here and able to see.”

“He’s an icon,” Daviss told Entertainment Tonight. “I really wanted to get down to who he was as a person, a loving person, and why people gravitate towards him and what that is about him, and it’s been amazing just getting to explore that as an actor.  I can wait for y’all to see what we do.”

title: Mariska Hargitay on the ‘Profoundly Healing’ Experience That’s Led to One of the Best Seasons of Her Life
summary: Mariska Hargitay opens up about the healing she found in making “My Mom Jayne,” hosting the Emmys and how Knicks point guard, Jalen Brunson, has inspired her.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.

In Hollywood, there are A-listers and then there’s royalty. Mariska Hargitay lands in the latter category. The daughter of screen legend Jayne Mansfield, Hargitay has followed in her mother’s footsteps, becoming luminary in her own right for her portrayal of Olivia Benson on “Law & Order: SVU.”
It’s a role that’s earned her both an Emmy and a Golden Globe. Not to mention that, at 27 years and counting, it’s the longest-running primetime series in NBC history.

On this day, however, Hargitay hasn’t come to unpack the latest season of the crime drama. Instead, we sit down in TODAY’s Orange Room to talk about the latest season of her life, a chapter that’s been especially fulfilling for a number of reasons.

Among them? She’s just wrapped her successful Broadway debut, sat courtside with bestie Taylor Swift before her beloved Knicks took home the championship, and premiered the deeply-personal film “My Mom Jayne,” which earned the 62-year-old yet another an Emmy nomination.

If she wins, she won’t have far to go to pick up the trophy since Hargitay is also hosting the Emmys this year, the first time a woman has hosted the awards show since Jane Lynch held the distinction back in 2011.

It’s undoubtedly Hargitay’s moment. The actor reflects on the “profound healing” that got her here and how the Knicks’ Jalen Brunson played a part in it. She also delves into her work with the Purple Leash Project, a partnership between Purina and the nonprofit RedRover that spotlights the need for more pet-friendly domestic violence shelters, an initiative near and dear to her heart.
This interview has been lighted edited for clarity.
First of all, I just want to acknowledge the fact that I didn’t think about it either and that’s what hit me so hard when I learned about it, because I don’t think anybody thinks about that.

So, it’s a really powerful and extraordinary initiative. Just the idea that a survivor shouldn’t have to choose between her safety and her animals. There’s already so many barriers of why not to leave and why not to go, but this one is a huge one.

This idea that pets are actually family members and oftentimes the most consistent, steady presence in a survivor’s life, that provides so much comfort, so much support, so much safety, really. And here was a reason that people weren’t going.

Up to 50% of survivors were not wanting to go, to leave their animals. So, it’s actually a brilliant initiative to a way of  supporting survivors. It takes that off their plate and they’re doing it all over and I was just so moved by it and so happy to get on board.

They’re like your children. They are an extended part of your family. Also, the idea of animals being used as threats or used as tactics to keep the person there or threaten that if they leave, they’ll hurt the animal. More than 70% of women in shelters report that their abuser has used an animal as a form of control.
So, it’s innovative, brilliant and so survivor-centric. And it is truly something that supports healing and gives survivors the courage to leave and supports them in a profound way.

I’ll tell you what it feels like: When I made this film, everything changed. I think the way I described it is finding so much more internal space that I didn’t have. It really settled my nervous system and was very profoundly healing for me in ways I was aware of, and in ways that I wasn’t.

My friend Kelli Giddish, my amazing co-star, had said to me after she saw (“My Mom Jayne”), because she knows me very well, she says, “I can’t wait to see what you do next,” and that really resonated with me really deeply.
For me, it wasn’t an accident that all this ... it was like a pathway started opening up because I think, and I’ve always believed, that the only way out is through. That’s sort of my motto.
This is also why I made this film, this is why I did that. Because I was carrying something that I didn’t want to carry and I realized, wasn’t mine to carry.

So, in a way, yes, I’m doing all these amazing things and I’m doing all these new things. In a way, it’s surprising and sort of unbelievable. And in a way, it feels like, “Of course. Now.” Because I’ve gotten ready for it internally.

I’ve always been a person to take on new challenges, but the fact that these opportunities are coming – I think that something shifted. So when the play came, I was 62. My mother was 22 (when she made her Broadway debut), and I made this film. So, I just believed that it wasn’t an accident that after I made the film, it sort of cleared that out and dealt with it and had a new reconciliation and new peace with it and so much new discovery.
So, the fact that the play came, I went, “Of course it did.” And I feel a little bit like that with the Emmys. As much as it was a shocker for me, I went, “Got it.”

Even Jalen (Brunson), all the Knicks stuff, that’s been so fun and exciting and he really is like my excellence mentor or my teacher of what’s possible in a very similar way that my dad was for me. I think that’s what also I love about him because my dad said, “You can do anything, you just have to set your mind to it.” That’s how I was raised.

So, when I see what Jalen has accomplished with the odds he goes up against, and his work ethic, and the fact that he holds a space to win, always, always, there’s no quitting ever with him, which is what my dad taught me.

It’s like, we don’t quit in this family. We keep going. It depends how much you want it. So it’s sort of this beautiful duality, that on one hand it’s, “Oh my gosh.” And on the other hand, it feels natural and I’m excited and ready in a way.

title: ‘Rest in Peace Ice Princesses’: A Generation Grapples with Hayden Panettiere and Michelle Trachtenberg’s Deaths
summary: Across social media, a generation is mourning the loss of “Ice Princess” stars Hayden Panettiere and Michelle Trachtenberg less than two years apart.
story: Across social media, a generation is mourning the loss of “Ice Princess” stars Hayden Panettiere and Michelle Trachtenberg less than two years apart.

Panettiere was found dead at age 36 in Greenville, South Carolina, on Aug. 16, according to local police. Her father confirmed her death in a statement. The case is under investigation, though police say there are no signs of “foul play or suspicious circumstances” at this time.
Panettiere’s death comes 18 months after Michelle Trachtenberg was found dead at age 39 in February 2025. The cause of death was later confirmed to be complications from diabetes.

Both Panettiere and Trachtenberg got their start in Hollywood as child actors. Panettiere played the kid daughter of coach Bill Yoast in 2000’s “Remember the Titans,” while Trachtenberg starred in the titular role 1996’s “Harriet the Spy,” opposite Rosie O’Donnell.
But it’s their roles in the 2005 Disney film “Ice Princess” that people came back to after their deaths.
“rest in peace to these ice princesses,” one X user wrote Aug. 17.
“I can’t believe they’re both gone,” one TikTok user captioned a compilation of clips of Panettiere and Trachtenberg together in the film.
Accompanying a photo of the pair from “Ice Princess,” another account wrote, “This picture is so incredibly sad now. Two actresses both gone way too young.”

Tim Fywell, the director of “Ice Princess,” said in a statement to Variety that Panettiere and Trachtenberg had “very different personalities.” Panettiere was “determined and perfectionist” while Trachtenberg was “kooky, fun, with an infectious laugh.”
“I remember them both with huge affection, how they were 20 odd years ago, at that relatively uncomplicated time of their lives, two shining talents, gone far too soon,” he said.

Trachtenberg starred in “Ice Princess” as Casey Carlyle, a physics student prodigy bound for Harvard with a secret passion for figure skating. Despite her mom Joan’s (Joan Cusack) protests, she starts to train, where she meets Gen Harwood, the de facto leader of a clique of teen figure skaters, played by Panettiere.

What is set up as a standard rivalry takes a twist, as Gen and Casey build a genuine friendship. It’s Gen’s mom, trainer and rink manager Tina (Kim Cattrall), who sabotages Casey to favor her own daughter. When Gen finds out, she walks away from the competition and tries to make amends with Casey.
“Rest in peace sweet Hayden. Gone far too soon,” Cattrall wrote on Instagram Aug. 17, alongside a photo of her and Panettiere in character as mother and daughter.
The movie, released by Disney, underperformed at the box office but stuck with millennials and Gen Z through showings on Disney Channel, becoming a nostalgic cult classic.

Several figure skaters have since cited the film as the inspiration that brought them to the sport. Zahra Lari, a skater from Abu Dhabi, said seeing the film at age 11 put her on her path toward eventually competing in Olympic qualifiers, per the Washington Post. In March 2025, HuffPost, in honor of the film’s 20th anniversary, hailed it a film that “helped a generation of girls gain confidence.”
Panettiere spoke about Trachtenberg to EW in September 2025, revealing her grandparents lived across the street from her co-star’s grandma in Brooklyn.

“We not only grew up in the same industry, but grew up knowing each other’s families, relatively closely, just because of the distance,” she said. “We would have block parties. So I have memories of her and I from long ago.”

“It was great to work with her,” she added. “... It was such a unique experience. I mean, we had to learn how to figure-skate in six weeks, which is no easy feat. But it was so much fun. We had a lot of fun and I’m very grateful that I have the memories that I have with her.”
After Trachtenberg’s death in 2025, one social media trend featured ice skaters perform to Aly and AJ’s “No One,” the marquee song used in the opening titles of “Ice Princess.”
“ice princess quite literally shaped my entire childhood growing up and now both actress who stared in that very film are now longer here. this so incredibly sad omg,” one X user said Monday.

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Reveals the Top 4 Dancers Heading to the Semifinals After Latest Elimination
summary: In Episode 6 of “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro,” the five remaining contestants were tasked with teaching an amateur. Find out who went home on Aug. 17.
story: With the finale quickly approaching, “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” is narrowing down its list of remaining contestants to just four after the latest elimination.

In Episode 6 of the competition series, out Aug. 17, the five potential pros — Adele Zaikman, AJ Pritchard, Allen Genkin, Nina Mayster and Selena Hamilton — were tasked with their most difficult challenge yet: teaching an amateur.
As all “Dancing With the Stars” fans know, helping a partner with limited dance knowledge learn a routine in a short amount of time is one of the most important skills a pro needs to possess.

Pro and two-time winner Witney Carson, who won the Mirrorball Trophy with host Robert Irwin last “DWTS” season, was announced as the guest judge for this week’s episode. She arrived in the ballroom and performed a seductive routine before explaining the challenge. (Her appearance comes as Carson announced that she is currently expecting her third child and will still compete on the upcoming fall season of “DWTS” alongside partner Guillermo.)

“This is a pro’s most testing role, and being great at it is just nonnegotiable,” she told the contestants. She informed them that they would each be paired with a “DWTS” fan and teach them a ballroom routine in just two days.
Dancing together this week…

Adele and social media influencer Anthony Riccardo dancing the tangoAJ and social media influencer Bailey McKnight dancing the Viennese waltzAllen and social media influencer Zaira Yzabelle dancing the waltzNina and social media influencer Jay Wyson dancing the foxtrotSelena and social media influencer Jeremy Urann dancing the quickstep
Adele and social media influencer Anthony Riccardo dancing the tango
AJ and social media influencer Bailey McKnight dancing the Viennese waltz
Allen and social media influencer Zaira Yzabelle dancing the waltz
Nina and social media influencer Jay Wyson dancing the foxtrot
Selena and social media influencer Jeremy Urann dancing the quickstep
While all the influencers had some dance experience, none of them had any previous ballroom training.
Read on to find out which contestants made sure their partners nailed the choreography, and which dancer was eliminated.
What Happened During Episode 6 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?
Seconds into rehearsals, each contestant demonstrated their unique coaching styles.
Adele told Anthony and the cameras that she sets a high bar for herself and her partner. He noted her strict instructions when chatting about his progress.

Selena, who has a background as a commercial dancer, revealed that she had never taught a quickstep before. Jeremy voiced concerns that the routine didn’t highlight any of his skills. So, Selena added some twists and turns to show off his personality and strengths.
As for Allen, he opted for a more gentle teaching style. He said he wanted to keep his routine simple to help Zaira, who shared she was used to faster steps.
“AJ’s teaching style is fast,” Bailey said in her confessional interview. He shared that he has nearly 20 years of teaching experience and knows what each student needs to succeed.
Unlike her fellow competitors, Nina spent her first day with Jay perfecting his frame instead of going over the choreography.

After the second day of rehearsals, which included a check-in from Witney and judges Mark and Shirley Ballas, the influencers enjoyed a night out. Witney joined them and asked how confident they felt about their routines on a scale of one to 10. Jeremy was the most confident (8) and Anthony was the least confident (4).

On performance day, Nina and Jay were up first. Shirley complimented Jay’s personality but said there were “fundamental issues” with the hold and footwork. Mark agreed that the frame was incorrect. Witney said she enjoyed the fun hip-hop moments in the routine but noted that Nina could’ve managed her time better in rehearsals.

Adele and Anthony’s performance followed. Mark applauded Adele’s “ambitious” routine. Shirley said she liked that Adele was fierce and fair, but pointed out that her teaching style could’ve used more “fun.” Witney said she was shocked by Anthony’s performance considering he was lacking confidence the night prior.

Taking the ballroom floor next were AJ and Bailey. Witney loved the routine but said she wished AJ would’ve included an emotional moment. Mark said it was clear Bailey felt comfortable. Shirley said they “absolutely killed it.”

Up fourth were Allen and Zaira. Shirley told the two that their partnership was “filled with beauty” even though some of the footwork wasn’t perfect. Witney said she noticed the trust between Allen and Zaira. Mark praised Allen and said he did a fantastic job.

Selena and Jeremy were the last pair to take the stage. Witney complimented Jeremy’s energy and said that although she liked Selena’s choreography, it was lacking enough quickstep content. Mark agreed with the feedback and said that a quickstep should travel around the ballroom floor. Shirley said the “character” of the quickstep was missing.
Who Was in the Bottom 2?

The two dancers in jeopardy were Nina and Selena. Mark said both dancers did well but they lacked “floor craft.” He said their dances should’ve covered more space on the ballroom floor to allow their partners to shine. Shirley said it seemed both ladies lacked ballroom knowledge.
Who Was Eliminated on Episode 6 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?
Shirley revealed that Nina had danced her final dance.

“It sucks. It hurts. But ... I haven’t cried like this in a while,” Nina said in her last confessional. She said she was leaving the competition better than she arrived and knows her worth now. She thanked the judges for their time and knowledge.
What Will Happen Next Week?

In Episode 7, which will air Aug. 24, the show will welcome multiple “DWTS” pros for the semifinal. The top four contestants will have to perform two dances, one with a pro and another with a fellow contestant.
The teaser suggested that some contestants will butt heads with the pros while others will thrive.

title: Salma Hayek Becomes a Grandma and She’s Already Given the Baby a Mexican Nickname
summary: Salma Hayek showed off her grandchild, sharing a video of her cradling him and calling him “Panchito.”
story: Salma Hayek already loves being an abuela — and has given herself and the newborn a sweet nickname.
The actor became a grandma after stepson François Pinault Jr. and his wife, Lara Cosima Henckel von Donnersmarck, welcomed their first child together.

Hayek and husband François-Henri Pinault share 18-year-old daughter Valentina. Pinault is also father to Pinault Jr., 28, Mathilde Pinault, 25, and Augustin James Evangelista, 19, from previous relationships.

Sharing a first glimpse of Pinault Jr.’s newborn on her Instagram, Hayek posted a video of her cradling the baby while she spoke Spanish to him. The “Grown Ups” star shared that the little one is named after his father and grandfather — but has another name in mind for the baby.
“We are blessed to welcome the fourth living generation of Francois’,” she wrote. “Although I will call him Panchito. He seems to love it, and I cannot love him more.”
In Mexico, Panchito or Pancho is a common nickname for people named Francisco. The French equivalent of Francisco is François.
In Hayek’s video she asks little “Panchito” in Spanish, “What are you dreaming about?”
The baby coos and giggles in his sleep as she continues calling him by the moniker and speaking to him in Spanish. “Nos da mucha risa.”
When she calls him “chiquitito hermoso,” he smiles and continues to laugh in his sleep. She also calls herself “abue,” short for abuela or grandma in Spanish.
On Aug. 12, von Donnersmarck shared a slideshow filled with photos of her and her bundle of joy. It also included snaps of baby François with his father and one with Hayek holding him.
“my husband (the world’s coolest françois) and our son (the world’s cutest françois)… our first month as parents,” the new mom captioned her post, adding a hatching chick emoji.

Hayek has supported her stepchildren’s accomplishments over the years. When Augustin Evangelista graduated high school last year, she shared photos from the celebration and wrote how proud she was of him.
She also congratulated his mom, model Linda Evangelista, for the parenting milestone. Linda Evangelista welcomed her son in 2006 after a brief romance with Pinault.
In the comments section of her own post celebrating her son’s graduation, the supermodel wrote to Hayek, “Love you and all your support.”
In a 2017 Red magazine interview, Hayek shared how she “always wanted to have a lot of children” and how becoming a stepmother was a “blessing.”
“And I was not able to. My body, as a miracle, had one,” she said. “The huge blessing I’ve had is that my husband has three other children. So I have four. And they are all so different.”

title: ‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ Books 6 and 7 Titles and Covers Revealed by Sarah J. Maas
summary: Fans of the Maas-iverse can finally rejoice — titles and covers for the anticipated sixth and seventh books in the “A Court of Thorns and Roses” series have been revealed.
story: Fans of the Maas-iverse can finally rejoice — titles and covers for the anticipated sixth and seventh books in the “A Court of Thorns and Roses” series have been revealed.

Author Sarah J. Maas, whose romantasy books have become bestsellers many times over thanks to her loyal legions of readers, had made subtle changes to the art on her website overnight and also wiped her social media accounts — signals within many fandoms that something big is to come.

On Aug. 17, she finally dropped her news: covers, titles and more details about her next two novels, which Maas had already shared in the spring are within her “ACOTAR” series and coming Oct. 27, 2026, and Jan. 12, 2027.
Oct. 27, 2026: “A Court of Splintered Harmony”Jan. 12, 2027: “A Court of Forgotten Melody”
Oct. 27, 2026: “A Court of Splintered Harmony”
Jan. 12, 2027: “A Court of Forgotten Melody”

As for what and whom these books may be about, some details within this rollout could serve as hints. First, both of the books include subtitles on the cover art: Book 6 says “The Valkyrie Cycle: Movement I” and Book 7 says “The Valkyrie Cycle: Movements II & III.”
Plus, new blurbs about the books have been revealed by her publisher, Bloomsbury. Here are each of them.
What was broken will be remade.
Deep in the heart of the continent, Koschei the Deathless is stirring.

Though he’s been bound to a mountain lake for millennia, the insidious threat of his return now spreads across the Fae territories, attracting powerful allies hell-bent on reclaiming what was once theirs: the human lands.

The Night Court will not stand idly by while innocents are attacked. But with Prythian still piecing itself together in the wake of the devastating Hybern War, the task of uniting is proving more difficult by the day.
To make matters worse, those who rule and protect the Night Court are reeling from recent betrayals and revealed truths. The rifts dividing them seem insurmountable.

But to defeat Koschei’s creeping shadow, they must find a way back to each other and resurrect their former alliances. To survive, they must find a way to repair the splintered harmony all around them.
What was lost will be reclaimed.

Prythian might never be the same again. Traditional alliances are crumbling, and no amount of diplomacy seems sufficient to repair them. With the continued threat of Koschei the Deathless on the horizon, a united front is crucial—and farther out of reach than it has ever been before.
Bonds will be tested. Power will shift. And old enemies will emerge from nightmares of the past.

As the Night Court’s Inner Circle disperses far and wide, desperate for any advantage against Koschei and his mighty allies, peace hangs by a fragile thread. But hope can be spun from the darkest of shadows, and the Night Court has its own part to play in the looming crescendo.

In tandem with the release of the book titles and cover art, digital billboards across Los Angeles, Denver and New York City went live to promote them, according to a press release from Maas’ team. And the hunch fans had about her digital presence was correct, too, as Maas’ team said her site and Instagram page will have a coordinated rebrand.

Maas is the author of 16 books across three different romantasy series: “ACOTAR,” as well as “Throne of Glass” and “Crescent City.” (For those in need of a reading guide, we’ve got you covered here.) Though she last published a book in 2024 — “House of Flame and Shadow,” a “Crescent City” book — her readers have been eager for the next installment of “ACOTAR,” a series that’s often the gateway into the rest of her universe.
In March, Maas did a rare sit-down interview on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast and revealed the release dates for these next two books. She also said these two books are part of a four-piece story.
“I like to do parts: part one, part two, part three,” Maas said. “By the time I got to the end of part one, it was, like, 400 pages long.”
“ACOTAR” 6 and 7 will tell the first three parts, she said, and the fourth and final part will come later.
“It’s meant to be read as one massive, massive story,” she said.
Prior to “Call Her Daddy,” Maas’ last interview was with us at TODAY in January 2024 when “House of Flame and Shadow” released. At the time, she said she had her next four books planned.

title: What Hayden Panetierre Shared About Her Brother Jansen, Who Died in 2023
summary: What happened to Hayden Panettiere’s brother, Jansen? What did he die of? Here’s what Hayden Panettiere said about her brother’s death.
story: Three years before her death at 36, Hayden Panettiere experienced the tragic loss of her younger brother.
Hayden Panettiere was found unresponsive by emergency personnel at a home in Greenville, S.C., on Aug. 16, according to a statement by the Greenville Police Department.

The death of the “Heroes” and Nashville” star followed the loss of her brother, Jansen Panettiere, in February 2023. He died of an undiagnosed heart condition, his family said in a statement to TODAY.com.
He was reported to be 28 at the time of his death. TODAY.com could not independently confirm his age.
Jansen Panettiere acted alongside his sister in the movies like “Tiger Cruise” and “Racing Stripes,” and also starred in “Ice Age: The Meltdown” and the AMC series “The Walking Dead.”
In the years after his death, Hayden Panettiere spoke about suffering such a devastating blow and also wrote about her brother’s loss in her recent memoir.
Here’s what she has shared about her brother’s life and death.
What Happened to Jansen Panettiere?
Jansen Panettiere died on Feb. 19, 2023, of an enlarged heart, his family said in a statement to TODAY.com.

“It is with great sorrow we share the tremendous, untimely loss of our beautiful Jansen,” the statement said. “Though it offers little solace, the Medical Examiner reported Jansen’s sudden passing was due to cardiomegaly (enlarged heart,) coupled with aortic valve complications.”

Cardiomegaly, or an enlarged heart, is not a disease itself, but is rather a sign of another condition, according to Mayo Clinic. Heart damage and certain types of heart disease can cause an enlarged heart, according to Mayo Clinic.
The Panettiere family did not specify the underlying cause of his condition, but said he suffered from aortic valve complications.
These complications can occur when the aorta, the main artery that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body, does not function properly, according to Mayo Clinic.

“Jansen’s heart could be seen in his eyes, and his charm in his brilliant, engaging smile; his soul in his masterful and revealing paintings, and the joy of life in his dry wit,” his family said in the statement. “His charisma, warmth, compassion for others, and his creative spirit will live forever in our hearts and in the hearts of all whom he encountered.”

“We sincerely appreciate the outpouring of love and support towards our family as we navigate this unthinkable loss, and ask that we be gifted our privacy during this time of mourning,” the family added. “We love you so much Jansen and you will be in our hearts forever.”
About a month before his death, he posted a black-and-white picture of his older sister styling his hair on Instagram.
“Not the first haircut she’s tried to give me,” he captioned the photo.
What Hayden Panettiere Said About Her Brother
Hayden Panettiere spoke on TODAY in September 2024 about trying to process her brother’s loss.
“I think it’s something that transforms over time,” she said.

“Maybe the five stages of grief is for people who have had a heartbreak or find out some bad news. Like, yes, there are five stages, but there’s so much more in between,” she continued. “And when you lose somebody that that you saw in all the important moments in your life, standing right next to you, it just rocks your world.”
Panettiere said at the time that her 2024 movie “Amber Alert” was dedicated to her brother.
“I want to leave this world a better place in his name,” she said.
She added that she thought having a conversation about grief and mental health “would be easier” than it has been.
“I had no idea how my body, my mind, was going to react to grief, and it’s wild, what stress and grief and all these hormones running through your body can do,” she said.
The actor spoke out about her brother’s death for the first time in an interview with People published on Sept. 18, about a week before her TODAY appearance.
“He was my only sibling, and it was my job to protect him,” she told the magazine. “When I lost him, I felt like I lost half of my soul.”
She said that in the days after her brother’s death, her body reacted in a way she had never seen before.
“Within days, I basically just like ballooned — ballooned out,” she said, adding that “stress and cortisol” can make changes to the body.
The changes, plus being followed by the paparazzi, made her not want to leave her house.

“I had to see horrific paparazzi pictures of myself coming out of Jansen’s funeral, which happened in a very private place, and it was shocking,” she said. “My agoraphobia came out, which is something I’ve struggled with in the past.”
She said it all compounded into diminishing her self-esteem.
“I didn’t feel confident to put on clothes and get out of the house, but I also knew that I needed to get out and keep moving or I’d never stop looking and feeling this way,” she said.
She added: “It became a destructive hamster wheel of, do I feel good enough to go out?”
The “Bring It On: All or Nothing” star eventually decided she wanted to go back to work, and she said everything changed when her publicist introduced her to her personal trainer.
“My body just started reacting, not just from the working out. It allowed me to release the stress, the high expectations I’d always put on myself,” she said.
Three months before her death, Hayden Panettiere cried on “The Jay Shetty Podcast” as she spoke about her brother.

“There’s nothing in my life that feels like losing my other half, the other half that was born to be the ying to my yang,” she said. “We were so close, and especially being the older sibling, it’s your job to protect them and keep them safe, and not being able to is — heartbreaking doesn’t even begin to cover it. I would need a dictionary to go through all the words for all the feelings that go through your mind.”
Panettiere was still processing his death three years after losing him.

“I collapsed, and it stayed with me,” she said. “Time is the best healer, generally, but it’s been three years and every year — it’s changed, the heartbreak has changed. But losing him and realizing how much of life I was going to have to go through alone and without him when I always saw him as being there.”
She described Jansen as her “best friend” and said she wants to call him “all the time.”

“When he first died, I just remember screaming, ‘I don’t want to live in a world where he doesn’t exist,’ so I’ve unfortunately had to,” she said. “But he seems so alive in my head still. He was such a big, big personality. He was just one of those people I never thought anything could take him down or take him away.

“He was so good, too, and it makes you so angry to see so that there are bad people thriving in this world, and then one so good that’s just taken from from you,” she continued. “Why? It’s not fair. It doesn’t make sense. I will never get over it. It will just evolve.”
Panettiere shared that her brother had a “serious” struggle with addiction and that she “begged” her parents to send him to military school before he was 18 years old due to those struggles.
Following his death, she said she kept several paintings done by her him.

“I feel him with me,” she said. “I know that he’s protecting me from where he is and is needed elsewhere, but I wish they would send him back to me. He was my rock. He was the only other person who fully understood everything about me.”

Panettiere writes candidly and movingly about their childhood together, her brother’s vibrant personality, their experiences as actors, his struggles with addiction and his death in her memoir “This is Me: A Reckoning,” released in May 2026.

She writes that in the time ahead of his death, she told her father that her brother had been using heroin and other drugs. On the day he died, her father said Jansen had an appointment and did not show up, so someone called one of his friends to check on him. When the friend arrived, Jansen was “already gone,” Panettiere said her father told her.

Panettiere was in Los Angeles ahead of the premiere of “Scream VI,” which marked her return to acting after four years away. She writes that her father asked her to call her mother and tell her the news. She honored his request.
“I hung up the phone, and the calm that helped me get through the call with Mom vanished,” she wrote. “I burst into tears, crawled into bed, and didn’t get out for the rest of the day.”
She ends her memoir with a tribute to her younger brother.
“Thank you for being here, Jansen, I thought. Thank you for making me laugh, telling me never to take myself too seriously, and for being my best friend, always,” she writes in the final sentence.
Panettiere also mentions him in the acknowledgments section, calling him “the heartbeat of my life, always right there, in the center of who I am.”
Earlier in the book, she reflects on having paintings by her brother as keepsakes.

“While seeing his life’s work breaks my heart all over again, I’m grateful to have something of him to hold on to,” she writes. “Learning to live in a world where he doesn’t exist has often brought me to my knees, but he would want me to remember that death and loss are a part of life, but they allow rebirth if you let them.”

title: USS Lincoln heads home after extended deployment to the Middle East
summary: Service members and their families had complained about deteriorating morale on the ship as its mission was extended to support the Iran war.
story: The USS Abraham Lincoln is on its way back home following an extended nine-month deployment, a U.S. official told NBC News on Thursday.
The U.S. official said the ship has been sailing for a few days and is expected to arrive back in San Diego in a few weeks.

With the Lincoln’s departure from the Middle East, where it was supporting the U.S. war against Iran, the USS George Washington arrived in the region Wednesday to begin a deployment, according to U.S. Central Command.
CENTCOM’s commander, Adm. Brad Cooper, said in an op-ed in The Wall Street Journal on Sunday that he visited the crew of the Lincoln on Saturday to announce their return home.
“I delivered the words every deployed sailor and Marine longs to hear: ‘You have delivered a performance for the ages, and now you are going home,’” Cooper wrote.

The Lincoln, which has been at sea for more than 250 days, has 5,000 sailors and Marines on board. The deployment has been marred by reports of deteriorating conditions. Cooper downplayed the concerns in the op-ed.
Add to Google
Add to Google

Relatives of those on board have told NBC News that conditions have been grim, citing a lack of supplies and food and a rising concern for worsening mental health. There have been some “man overboard” incidents, including one in which a sailor was rescued, according to U.S. officials. While the incidents have raised concerns within the Navy, they have not been viewed as reflective of a broad mental health crisis aboard the carrier, according to a U.S. official.

The mother of a sailor aboard the Lincoln told NBC News that her son was expecting to be deployed for six months. When she finally heard from him, about a month after the Feb. 28 strikes, she said, he mentioned he was hungry and losing weight. He told his mother the Lincoln’s onboard commissary was limiting service members’ purchases.

“He was just eating what he could eat,” she said, adding that he said the hot water was sometimes out for days and that the crew members went three to four months without getting mail after the carrier was redirected from the South China Sea.
The mother, a former service member herself, said her son told her that there were people “who weren’t doing too well.”
“One person had just given up; they weren’t reporting for duty. They were wanting to get sent home,” she said. “I could tell his voice was sounding like he was down.”

She acknowledged that safety and the conditions in the region could have been the reason for the historic number of consecutive days at sea. According to her son, things got briefly better in April after parents started complaining about the ship’s conditions.
The mother said she is very proud of everyone who has served on the Lincoln and hopes they are able to get the resources they need.
“Everyone needs to be treated with decency regardless of the job,” she said.
Cooper, the CENTCOM commander, said concerns about issues had been addressed.
Cooper wrote Sunday on social media that of the Navy’s 11 active aircraft carriers, the Lincoln “currently has among the lowest number of cases related to mental health.”

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said last week that reports about the situation aboard the Lincoln have been “completely misrepresented.” President Donald Trump also dismissed concerns last week, telling reporters Friday that the deployment was “not nearly long enough.”

The Lincoln left San Diego on Nov. 21, and its deployment was planned to end in May. It was extended as the U.S. remained embroiled in the war against Iran, which began with U.S. and Israeli strikes at the end of February. A typical deployment for a carrier is roughly six to seven months; the Lincoln has been deployed for nine months.

Carriers also usually make regular stops at ports to refresh and replenish food supplies during those deployments. The Lincoln has not visited a port since December, according to a U.S. official, marking over 200 days consecutively at sea.

title: Prince Harry and Meghan will move back to the United Kingdom
summary: The couple has lived in California since 2020. King Charles was informed of the move Sunday, a source said.
story: Prince Harry and his family will leave the sunny shores of Southern California and return to the United Kingdom, a source familiar with the couple’s plans said.
The Duke of Sussex, 41, and his wife, Meghan, 45, along with their two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, have been living in Montecito, an affluent coastal enclave in Santa Barbara County.
King Charles was informed of the move on Sunday, a source familiar with the couple’s plans told NBC News. The matter was not discussed during the Sussexes’ visit in July, The Telegraph reported.

King Charles welcomes the opportunity to see more of the Sussex family in a private capacity, but maintains that they will remain private individuals and nonworking members of the royal family, the source said.
A spokesperson for the couple declined to comment on reasons for the move.
The couple took refuge in the Golden State after stepping back from royal duties in 2020.
The Telegraph and The Sun were the first to report the move Wednesday evening.
The reports said Archie and Lilibet have been enrolled in British schools to start in September, meaning the family will likely move within the next two weeks.
Harry and Meghan, however, will not return to royal duties, nor will they live in a royal residence, opting for a more private life.
It remains unclear what security — a point of great contention in the past between the prince and the royals — will look like.

On the question of Harry and Meghan’s security arrangements, a U.K. Home Office spokesperson said, “It is our long-standing policy not to provide detailed information on those arrangements, as doing so could compromise their integrity and affect individuals’ security.”
Meghan is expected to continue to run her lifestyle brand, As Ever, while living in the U.K.

The move back across the pond comes on the heels of Harry’s contentious visit to the U.K. in July — where his offer to stay at Buckingham Palace was rescinded and he had to walk back initial plans to travel with his wife and children over security concerns.
Prior to July, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex were last together in the U.K. in 2022, for the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II.

A royal family reunion may not be a smooth affair given Harry’s strained relationship with his father, King Charles, and elder brother, Prince William, for the past few years. Harry aired some of his grievances in his 2023 memoir “Spare” and has spoken publicly about tensions within the family.
Last year, Harry met with his father, who is undergoing treatment for cancer, after he had claimed the monarch refused to speak with him.
Despite the frosty relationship, Harry expressed a desire to reconcile with his family in May 2025, noting he did not “know how much longer my father has.”
India McTaggart, a royal correspondent at The Telegraph, told NBC News that moving to the U.K. has been a longtime wish of Harry’s.

“He’s made, you know, no secret of his intention to want to bring his children here to reunite them with the king, his father, and the Spencer side of the family, and just have a place where he can come to the U.K. without the circus of his arrival,” McTaggart said.
She said that while Harry’s relationship with his brother, Prince William, remains fraught as they “haven’t spoken in years,” Harry has “started speaking to the king, his father, a lot more.”
Moving back to the U.K. may also be an easier decision for the family given Harry’s charity work there.

“A lot of his charities are based here, whether it’s Invictus or WellChild. And I think he feels closer to home here, obviously, because friends are here and I think it’s become so deeply complicated for him to go back and forth because of all the security concerns he had,” McTaggart said. “I just think he has sort of wanted to do this for a while, and it appears that Meghan is taking one for the team.”

title: U.S. military drills with South Korea are cut short after surprise order
summary: The annual U.S.-South Korea drills, known as Ulchi Freedom Shield, will end Aug. 21 rather than Aug. 27 as originally scheduled, both countries said.
story: Joint military exercises underway between the United States and South Korea are being cut short, both countries said, after President Donald Trump ordered that they be reduced and cited his “very good” relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
The surprise announcement drew suggestions that Trump may want to revive his bid to strike a grand bargain with Kim over his isolated regime’s nuclear arsenal.
Trump is open to a new meeting with Kim at the “appropriate time,” a White House official told NBC News, but no date has been set and no formal planning has started on a potential visit.

The president is expected to travel to Asia this fall to attend several summits, including the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gathering in Shenzhen, China, in November, but it’s unclear whether any possible meeting would be set up around that timeframe.

However, Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong dampened hopes for a resumption of diplomacy between Trump and her brother, saying she was not aware of any communication between the two nations in comments carried by state media.

Regarding the curtailment of the U.S.-South Korea drills, “we think it’s not worth making comments on that and we have no interest in it,” she said. “The provocative, aggressive nature of the drills won’t change even though their duration and size were reduced.”

Trump, who met with Kim three times during his first term in office, has mused publicly about resuming their earlier diplomacy, which collapsed in 2019. The Wall Street Journal was first to report the possible Kim meeting.

After Trump’s public order to scale back the annual U.S.-South Korea drills, known as Ulchi Freedom Shield, the exercises will now end Aug. 21 rather than Aug. 27 as originally scheduled, a Defense Department official said.
“Associated live-training events have been reduced, with certain events canceled or converted to simulations,” the official said, adding that the adjustments “preserve essential readiness.”
“There will be no degradation to U.S. training objectives,” the official said.
Trump orders reduction of joint exercises with South Korea
The South Korean National Defense Ministry also said the two countries “have agreed, at the request of the U.S. side, to make some adjustments to the duration and scale of the exercise.”

Some of the combined field training exercises will be conducted on a reduced scale, the ministry said in a statement, adding that the U.S. and South Korea “are currently consulting on the specific details.”

“Going forward, the ROK and the United States will discuss and implement various measures to achieve the objectives of the UFS exercise and maintain a robust combined defense posture,” the ministry said, using an abbreviation for South Korea’s formal name, the Republic of Korea.
The ministry declined to comment on a reported meeting Tuesday between Gen. Xavier Brunson, the commander of U.S. Forces Korea, and South Korean Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back.

The surprise comments by Trump, which he made on social media hours before the exercises began Monday, have unsettled South Korea, which relies heavily on the U.S. for its security, as well as other U.S. allies in the region facing a growing threat from nuclear-armed North Korea.

South Korean Foreign Affairs Minister Cho Hyun said Ahn had been “in close consultation with the U.S. side” since Trump’s social media post. He told lawmakers Wednesday that “neither our government nor officials in the U.S. government had any prior knowledge” of Trump’s order to scale back the drills.

According to U.S. Forces Korea, the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise with South Korea, which hosts 28,000 American troops, aims to build understanding between the two militaries to ensure their “ability to fortify the combined defense posture” and enhance their response to “a spectrum of security threats.”
Foremost among those threats is North Korea, which in recent years has advanced its missile and nuclear capabilities and developed a close security relationship with Russia.
Though the U.S. and South Korea say their drills are defensive in nature, North Korea routinely criticizes them as a rehearsal for invasion and often test-fires weapons in protest.
In his post Sunday, Trump said the exercises sent a “totally inappropriate and hostile” message to North Korea, which he said had been “unthreatening and respectful” during his time in office.
He also expressed anger over South Korea’s level of involvement in the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and said he had ordered Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to “substantially reduce” the exercises.

Kim, whose position has strengthened considerably since Trump’s first term, has rebuffed recent overtures from the U.S. president as well as South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, saying he will not come to the table unless they drop their demands for North Korea to denuclearize first.
Trump told reporters Monday that he was not sacrificing the security of U.S. allies to curry favor with North Korea and that he was “actually making it much safer.”
He said Kim had responded to his outreach, without providing details. “I understand him; he understands me,” Trump said.

title: China’s backflipping robots leap to blockbuster stock market debut in latest sign of AI boom
summary: Unitree’s shares closed up 460% on Wednesday, a significant marker as Beijing competes with Washington for global tech dominance.
story: HONG KONG — The robotics firm behind China’s famously backflipping humanoids leaped to a remarkable stock market debut Wednesday, with Unitree’s shares closing up 460% as investors rally behind homegrown beneficiaries of the AI boom.

Chinese humanoid and other robots have advanced at a breathtaking pace as Beijing competes for global tech dominance with Washington, which banned imports of new foreign-made robots last month over national security concerns. Unitree, the first humanoid robotics maker to go public on a mainland Chinese exchange, has won global attention with its humanoid and quadruped robots that can run, dance and do backflips and kung fu.

On Monday, the Hangzhou-based company unveiled its “Superman” robot, which it says can jump more than 6.5 feet high and has a top speed of more than 28 mph — faster than men’s 100-meter world record holder Usain Bolt.

Unitree’s stock, which was initially priced at 150.8 yuan ($22) a share, closed Wednesday at 845 yuan ($125.40) on Shanghai’s tech-focused STAR Market, valuing the company at about $50 billion. Earlier, it went as high as 1,100 yuan ($163.23), or 629%.
Add to Google
Add to Google
The debut leaves Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing, who owns about a fifth of the company he founded in 2016, with wealth on paper of more than $12 billion, according to Reuters.
Though Unitree is profitable, unlike most of its competitors, its products are mainly being sold to universities and research institutions rather than being used commercially.

And it is being cut off from the U.S. market under the ban, though existing models can continue to be sold. The U.S. accounted for about 13% of Unitree’s $250 million in revenue last year, according to its IPO prospectus.

In June, the U.S. Defense Department also added Unitree to a list of Chinese military companies, describing it as a “contributor to the Chinese defense industrial base.” Though the designation does not involve sanctions on Unitree, which says its robots are for civilian use only, it prohibits the U.S. military from contracting directly with it.

Hundreds of Chinese companies showed off new products at the World Robot Conference in Beijing, which started Wednesday. China is betting big on AI and robotics to help turbocharge its economy’s growth, which slowed to its weakest in over three years last quarter.

Beijing has put the advanced robotics industry front and center of its national agenda, with its latest five-year plan vowing to “target the frontiers of science and technology.” Unitree and AgiBot, another Chinese company, together accounted for more than 70% of the approximately 13,000 humanoid robots shipped globally last year, according to the Singapore-based market research firm Omdia.

Unitree’s debut follows another blockbuster listing in Shanghai by the Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT, which surpassed tech giant Tencent to become the most valuable company listed on a mainland Chinese exchange after its shares surged 466% on their first day of trading last month.
Investors championing Unitree and CXMT are riding on the wave of China’s growing prowess across the entire AI pipeline — from memory, which is crucial in data centers, to models to robotics.

“Chinese retail buyers tend to be more driven by hype,” said Lian Jye Su, a chief analyst at Omdia. “But the most important thing about the IPO is the fact that this is going to be the bellwether for the humanoid robotics industry.”
Unitree’s performance will be closely monitored as several other Chinese robotics companies prepare to go public.
“The industry is still in a very nascent stage,” Lian said. “The first thing I’m seeking an answer for is sort of how real is the demand.”

title: Kushner and Netanyahu agree U.S. general should oversee Hamas ‘demilitarization,’ source says
summary: The agreement came during an hourslong meeting, which followed rare talks between the leader of Hamas, Kushner and other members of Trump’s Board of Peace.
story: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner on Monday agreed that the Gaza Strip’s “demilitarization” should start with a Hamas weapons handover supervised by an American military general, according to a senior Israeli official.

The agreement came during an hourslong meeting, which followed rare talks between the leader of Hamas, Kushner and other members of Trump’s Board of Peace — part of a renewed push to revive a Gaza peace plan endorsed by Trump and Hamas but rejected by Israel.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the details of the meeting provided by the senior Israeli official.
U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee and former British Prime Minister Tony Blair joined Netanyahu and Kushner.

Netanyahu and Kushner also agreed that no reconstruction of Gaza should begin before Hamas is disarmed and that “necessary measures” should be taken to “address sanitation and environmental concerns,” the official added.
Netanyahu “made it clear” that the Israel Defense Forces will not redeploy but that it will “continue to thwart” threats to its forces and the residents of Israel, the official said.
The group “held deep and constructive discussions on the way forward,” a Board of Peace official told NBC News.

They agreed the IDF would not redeploy from Gaza until Hamas is fully disarmed and agreed to immediately establish joint working groups on the demilitarization of Gaza and the basic needs of the Palestinian enclave including clean water, the Board of Peace official said.
Add to Google
Add to Google
In a statement, Netanyahu’s office did not confirm the details given by the Israeli official but did confirm that the group had agreed to establish the two working groups.
Both Israel and the Board of Peace agree that the disarmament and demilitarization piece “should be prompt and completed before any reconstruction happens in Gaza,” the prime minister’s office said.

The U.S. and Israel have shown rare public divisions over the road map for the future of the Palestinian enclave, as well as the Israeli government’s approach to a mounting crisis in the occupied West Bank.

The renewed diplomatic effort comes as Netanyahu faces growing domestic pressure ahead of Israeli elections in October, including from the far-right faction upon which his fragile coalition government relies.

Netanyahu earlier this month rejected Trump’s 15-point plan, which would require Hamas’ disarmament and Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza, with the Israeli leader vowing that there would be no military pullout until Hamas is “genuinely disarmed.”

title: Canada races to avoid new U.S. tariffs of up to 50%
summary: The duties would hit a wide swath of goods, including hockey sticks, building materials, clothing and dairy products.
story: The Canadian government is racing to negotiate a deal with the Trump administration in order to avoid a fresh wave of U.S. tariffs set to hit many of its exports to the United States starting on Wednesday.
However, after weeks of meetings, the prospects for a deal remained uncertain Monday, and Canadian broadcaster CBC reported that the two countries were at an impasse.
Speaking to reporters, Prime Minister Mark Carney described the talks as “very delicate and intense.” He also said he planned to speak with Trump before the deadline.

The new tariffs, if implemented, would hit about $20 billion worth of Canadian products imported to the U.S., including hockey sticks, some clothing, wines, some dairy products and certain building materials such as cement and plywood. Energy products, potash, fish and critical minerals are excluded from the duties.
In 2025, Canada ranked as the third-largest source of imports for the U.S., according to Census Bureau data, with more than $380 billion worth of goods crossing the border into the U.S. last year.

The White House has said the tariffs are in response to Canada’s “discriminatory treatment of American products” and that it’s “leveling the playing field for crucial American exports — cars, alcohol, and dairy.”

It plans to implement the duties under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, a 96-year-old law that authorizes the president to hit any foreign country that discriminates against U.S. commerce with tariffs of up to 50%.
No president has ever invoked Section 338 before, and legal challenges are all but certain to be filed against the tariffs.
